CHIEF COMPLAINT
Yearly exam

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Beverly is a 24-year-old female with a history of type 2 diabetes and hypertension presenting for her yearly examination. She reports doing well overall. She began working in a bakery this summer and has been enjoying the job. However, she notes that proximity to baked goods and desserts has led to increased snacking and consumption of sweets during work shifts. She attributes her recent poor blood sugar control to dietary changes related to her new job, though she reports taking her diabetes medication as prescribed without any missed doses. She describes it as challenging to resist the temptation of the treats at work. Blood pressure has been well-controlled despite fluctuating blood sugars. She reports sleeping well with full eight hours nightly. She denies any concerning thoughts of self-harm.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
No additional concerns beyond those discussed. Status quo except for dietary issues related to work environment.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Type 2 diabetes mellitus
Hypertension
Systolic ejection murmur (grade 2, unchanged from prior)

MEDICATIONS
Metformin twice daily
Lisinopril 10 mg once daily

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Currently employed in a bakery since summer. Works in close proximity to baked goods and desserts.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Neurological: Grip strength equal bilaterally. Sensation intact. Motor function intact with good leg strength. Neurovascular exam intact.
Cardiovascular: Heart regular rate and rhythm. Grade 2 systolic ejection murmur present, unchanged from prior. No carotid bruits. Pulses good.
Pulmonary: Lungs clear to auscultation.
General: No thyromegaly. No edema.
Overall: Essentially normal exam.

RESULTS
Hemoglobin A1c: Elevated
Blood pressure: Good, within normal limits

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus - out of control. Hemoglobin A1c elevated. Target A1c under 7%, preferably under 6%. Continue current metformin therapy. No medication changes at this time as this appears diet-related. Patient to cut down on snacking and additional sweets. Patient to check fasting blood sugars in the morning and call in results in approximately two weeks. Follow-up visit in two months to reassess. If blood sugars have not improved, will consider adding additional antidiabetic medication.

2. Hypertension - stable and well-controlled. Continue lisinopril 10 mg once daily. No changes to current regimen.
